requirement:
The coverage index MUST display the combined view selected under
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.index.selection` and
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.index.freshness`. It MUST identify the
contributing runs and show each selected test's binary, test name, attempt,
capture time, command, selection, and outcome, including missing or stale
coverage. It MUST show source revisions and uncommitted-source state when
available rather than present records from several runs as one run.

For first-party Rust files under
{cite}`requirements.references.rust_item_coverage`, the summary MUST compute
line coverage from the union of instrumented file-and-line locations in the
selected fresh records, including their associated child-process records.
Each location MUST count once in the denominator and count as covered when any
selected record has a positive execution count for it. Percentages MUST be
computed from those union counts rather than averaged across process reports.
A view with no instrumented lines MUST show coverage as unavailable. The index
MUST link to {cite}`requirements.test-coverage.index.details`, visibly identify
incomplete coverage, and MUST NOT imply that every current test has coverage
merely because all available records are valid.
rationale:
The four tests marked `{test}` for `requirements.test-coverage.index.summary` cover the obligations assessed here. They are all in `src/execution_coverage/book.rs`. The `selection`, `freshness` and `details` requirements are cited context. Their own tests and implementations were not reassessed.

**Union line coverage (child processes, once-per-location counting, union percentage)**
- `file_maps_union_process_locations_and_filter_unexecuted_test_files` builds a test process and a child process.
  - Both processes record counts for the same `code.rs` location. The test process has a positive count there and the child has zero.
  - The child also covers another `code.rs` location with a count of `u64::MAX`.
  - A zero-count `zero.rs` location adds to the denominator only.
  - It asserts `Line coverage: **2/4 (50.0%)**`. That result needs the shared location counted once in the denominator and covered when any record has a positive count. It also needs the child's extra location included.
  - A per-process average would give a different figure, so this assertion rules out averaging.
- `reports_identify_attempts_and_union_child_counts_without_discarding_profiles` unions a child's positive count with the test process's positive count on a different location. It asserts `2/2 (100.0%)`.
- `filtered_runs_union_latest_attempts_and_invalidate_with_saved_source` unions two filtered runs, each covering one of two locations. It asserts `2/2 (100.0%)`, where an average would give 50%.

**No instrumented lines → unavailable**
- `maps_distinguish_no_runs_zero_hits_stale_and_incomplete_coverage` covers two cases.
  - With no runs, it asserts `Coverage unavailable`.
  - With an empty record, it asserts `Coverage unavailable`, no `Line coverage:` text, no `NaN`, and `No usable instrumented lines`.

**Selected tests' fields, runs, revisions and dirty state**
- `file_maps_union_process_locations_and_filter_unexecuted_test_files` checks the provenance table for these fields:
  - `binary / one`
  - the `Attempt` and `Captured (Unix ns)` headers
  - `success / success`
  - the revision and dirty fields
  - `cargo nextest run`
  - `filtered`
- `reports_identify_attempts_and_union_child_counts_without_discarding_profiles` checks per-row contents for the attempt number, capture time, outcome and contribution.
  - It checks the run ID is shown.
  - It checks that revision and dirty state show when available, and as `unknown` when the run lacks them.
  - It checks the command and selection show as `cargo nextest run` / `filtered`.
  - Two different runs appear as separate rows, so records are not presented as one run.

**Missing or stale coverage shown, incomplete coverage visible, no over-claiming**
- `filtered_runs_union_latest_attempts_and_invalidate_with_saved_source` asserts these strings:
  - `unavailable: incomplete`, for failed and interrupted newest attempts.
  - `stale: source inputs changed or unavailable`.
  - `gap counts unavailable`.
- `maps_distinguish_no_runs_zero_hits_stale_and_incomplete_coverage` asserts stale and unavailable attempt counts and `Coverage history is incomplete`. It also asserts that unavailable coverage yields no coverage map, and that stale records give `Coverage unavailable`.
- `reports_identify_attempts_and_union_child_counts_without_discarding_profiles` asserts the text `not establish that all current tests were measured`. That text covers the clause that valid records must not imply every current test has coverage.

**Link to details**
- `reports_identify_attempts_and_union_child_counts_without_discarding_profiles` checks that the index links to each detail chapter via the computed `href`.
- `file_maps_union_process_locations_and_filter_unexecuted_test_files` checks that the test selector offers an option for the coverage report.

**Combined view selection**
- `filtered_runs_union_latest_attempts_and_invalidate_with_saved_source` shows records from an excluded build configuration as a `historical build configuration`, and the combined figure comes from the main configuration only.

**Remaining question: first-party scope**
Scoping to first-party Rust files, with root `vendor` excluded, is applied when coverage is exported in `src/execution_coverage/runner.rs`. It is not applied in the summary. That filtering belongs to other requirements, and the summary tests operate on recorded data.

I found no plausible requirement-violating behavior that these tests would accept, so I found no adequacy gap.

text: :::{req} index.summary
The coverage index MUST display the combined view selected under
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.index.selection` and
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.index.freshness`. It MUST identify the
contributing runs and show each selected test's binary, test name, attempt,
capture time, command, selection, and outcome, including missing or stale
coverage. It MUST show source revisions and uncommitted-source state when
available rather than present records from several runs as one run.
For first-party Rust files under
{cite}`requirements.references.rust_item_coverage`, the summary MUST compute
line coverage from the union of instrumented file-and-line locations in the
selected fresh records, including their associated child-process records.
Each location MUST count once in the denominator and count as covered when any
selected record has a positive execution count for it. Percentages MUST be
computed from those union counts rather than averaged across process reports.
A view with no instrumented lines MUST show coverage as unavailable. The index
MUST link to {cite}`requirements.test-coverage.index.details`, visibly identify
incomplete coverage, and MUST NOT imply that every current test has coverage
merely because all available records are valid.
:::{req} index.selection
The coverage index MUST combine the most recent recorded test attempt for each
nextest binary and test name among the retained runs. "Most recent" MUST refer
to when the attempt started, including failed or interrupted attempts. A newer
filtered run MUST update only the tests it executes, leaving other compatible
test records available to the combined view. A newer attempt with missing or
unreadable coverage MUST be shown as unavailable rather than replaced with an
older successful attempt. Results from incompatible instrumented build
configurations MUST NOT be combined under
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.storage.configuration`.
The main combined view MUST use the instrumented build configuration of the
most recently started recorded test attempt. Latest-per-test selection MUST
occur within that configuration. Records from other configurations MUST be
identified as excluded historical coverage. Configuration selection MUST use
recorded metadata without building or executing tests.
:::{req} index.freshness
Only records whose captured source inputs match the current project source and
whose build configurations are compatible MAY contribute execution counts to
the combined view of {cite}`requirements.test-coverage.index.selection`.
Records invalidated by a source change, or whose compatibility cannot be
established, MUST be identified as stale or unavailable and excluded from the
combined coverage totals. Their retained per-process reports MUST remain
inspectable using their captured source until the build artifacts are removed.
:::{req} rust_item_coverage

During repository validation, Habeas MUST parse every first-party Rust source file: every `.rs` file among the sources reference discovery considers under {cite}`requirements.references.discovery`, except those under the project-root `vendor` directory. Each explicitly declared function or method, including trait methods and test helpers, and each struct, enum, and union is an item that can be covered. An item is covered when it has a valid `{impl}`, `{cite}`, or `{test}` reference to a defined requirement or named example, or a valid citation of the built-in `habeas:util` under {cite}`requirements.references.util`, in a Rust comment attached to it or within its body; or when its outline node, or an outline node containing it, is recorded with its current hash as an outline input of an evidence record, a citation review, or a site review. Outline inputs recorded from selected search snippets under {cite}`requirements.authoring.finish_search.inputs` MUST count alongside mandatory inputs and additional reads. Comments belong to items under {cite}`requirements.references.outline_comments`; a comment before a field, variant, or attribute inside an item belongs to that item. A named example MUST reference a requirement under {cite}`requirements.examples.definition`. A reference in a string literal, on an enclosing module or impl block, or only in an evidence input MUST NOT count for the items it encloses. Habeas MUST report a Rust parse failure instead of silently skipping the file. Only {cite}`requirements.references.coverage.tests` and {cite}`requirements.references.coverage.examples` make an uncovered item a validation error; other items without recent coverage are warned about under {cite}`requirements.references.coverage.report`.
:::{req} index.details
For the records displayed by {cite}`requirements.test-coverage.index.summary`,
`habeas mdbook` MUST generate a detail subchapter under the execution-coverage
chapter of {cite}`requirements.test-coverage.index` for each recorded nextest
test process, identifying its binary, test name, attempt, test-attempt outcome,
and originating run. Each report MUST show its instrumented first-party Rust
source lines and execution counts, distinguishing executed from unexecuted
lines, using the source captured for that run, and link back to the
execution-coverage chapter.
Coverage from associated child processes MUST remain distinguishable from
coverage recorded by the nextest test process itself.
